title: Add Runtime LTS perf baseline + RC gating thresholds (p95 latency + throughput) with alert hooks
author: Allison Grant
description:
Context: As part of the Runtime LTS channel work, we need a repeatable perf suite baseline and enforceable gates for LTS release candidates. Enterprise customers (and our own SRE gates) care primarily about: (1) p95 latency not regressing beyond an agreed budget, and (2) throughput not dropping (or at least not dropping silently).

This PR adds:
- A first LTS baseline config (runtime-1.20-lts) for the perf-canary suite.
- Explicit gating thresholds for p95 latency and throughput for the LTS suite.
- Alerting hooks that fire for LTS RC runs (GitHub Check summary + Slack notification to #eng-sre and #eng-releases).

Key behavior:
- Gating is ONLY enforced when the run is marked as an LTS RC (either the workflow sets LTS_RC=true or the runtime version matches *-lts.*). This avoids blocking regular perf-canary development and non-LTS runtime trains.
- We gate on p95 end-to-end latency and throughput at the suite level, and we surface top 5 regressions at the scenario level for fast triage.
- p99 is computed and reported, but not currently used as a release gate (see discussion below).

Thresholds (initial):
- p95 latency regression budget: +3.0% (relative) vs baseline per scenario; +2.0% at suite aggregate.
- throughput regression budget: -2.5% (relative) vs baseline per scenario; -2.0% at suite aggregate.
- If either suite aggregate gate fails OR >=3 scenarios exceed the scenario-level budget, the run fails with a clear summary.

Alerting:
- GitHub: adds a check run summary with a table: baseline vs candidate, deltas, and the exact thresholds.
- Slack: posts a compact message with (a) pass/fail, (b) link to run, (c) suite aggregate deltas, (d) top regressions.
  - Default channels: #eng-sre, #eng-releases
  - Uses existing ci secret PERF_CANARY_SLACK_WEBHOOK (no new secret added).

Notes / follow-ups:
- This PR intentionally does NOT try to define the baseline dataset/versioning; it assumes the benchmark-lab baseline is stable and referenced by immutable IDs. See benchmark-lab PR #522 for the dataset pinning work.
- We should revisit the budgets after we get 2-3 RCs worth of noise/variance data. The budgets are conservative but intended to be actionable.

Why p95 and not p99 for gating?
- Based on recent LTS gate discussions, p99 is too noisy across GPU types/driver revisions to use as a hard gate right now. We still compute and display it (and will page if it spikes beyond a larger “watch” threshold in a later change).

Testing:
- Ran dry-run workflow on a known-good commit and validated it produces a green gate.
- Forced a synthetic +6% p95 regression via the test harness to validate failure mode and Slack formatting.

Release impact:
- No changes to production runtime; this is CI/release signal tooling. It will block LTS RC promotion if thresholds fail.

Refs:
- Linear: ENG-4827 (Perf regression gates for LTS), ENG-4824 (LTS CI workflow)
- Support context: SUP-3950 (customer requesting backport into LTS instead of upgrading after regression)

Checklist:
- [x] Thresholds documented and linkable from LTS release checklist
- [x] Clear failure summary for release managers (no hunting through raw logs)
- [x] Slack alert includes link + owner hints
- [x] Does not block non-LTS runs

Screenshots / examples (from dry-run): Gate summary shows Suite p95: +0.7% (PASS), Suite throughput: -0.4% (PASS); scenarios table includes top deltas and per-scenario budgets.
commits: Add LTS baseline config + schema fields for gating budgets
Implement gate evaluation (suite aggregate + scenario thresholds)
Add GitHub Actions step to annotate check summary and fail run on gate breach
Add Slack notifier for LTS RC runs (pass/fail + top regressions)
Docs: describe LTS gate semantics and how to override for investigation
review_conversation:
Sean Gallagher (SRE): Can we make it explicit that this only blocks LTS RC promotion and not every run? Also, can you include the suite aggregate criteria in the failure message?

Allison Grant (author): Yep. Added LTS_RC guard at the workflow level + runtime version matcher. Failure summary now includes suite aggregate deltas and the exact budgets.

Miles Thornton (SRE): I’m still worried about false positives on p99. Are we using p99 anywhere?

Allison Grant (author): Not for gating. p99 is computed and displayed, but the hard gate is p95 + throughput. Added a short rationale to docs/lts-gates.md. We can add a “watch threshold” + alert-only in a follow-up.

Sahana Iyer (Release Eng): Slack webhook usage is fine but please ensure it doesn’t run on forks / untrusted contexts. Also, make sure the check summary is readable for release managers.

Allison Grant (author): Updated workflow to only notify on push to trusted branches and when PERF_CANARY_SLACK_WEBHOOK is present. Also tightened the summary formatting (table + top regressions).

Connor O’Brien (Release Eng): Can we link this output directly from the LTS release checklist? And do we have an override mechanism for investigation (e.g., rerun without gating)?

Allison Grant (author): Added docs link (docs/lts-gates.md) and a workflow input to run in “report-only” mode for investigation. For actual RC promotion, checklist will require gating enabled.

Kira Volkov: Baseline naming: use runtime-1.20-lts not runtime-1.20.0-lts to match the branch semantics.

Allison Grant (author): Done; updated baseline ID and workflow matcher.

Sean Gallagher (SRE): Approved after last push. Please keep budgets visible in the message so we can explain failures quickly.

Allison Grant (author): Included budgets in both GitHub summary and Slack message.

Final: Approved by Sean, Miles, Sahana. Merged via squash.
release_notes: Adds Runtime LTS perf baseline (runtime-1.20-lts) for perf-canary.
Introduces RC gating thresholds for p95 latency and throughput with clear failure summaries.
Posts pass/fail + top regressions to #eng-sre and #eng-releases for LTS RC runs.
